tip: henüz means 'yet'. With a negative verb like gelmedi it means 'not yet': Onlar henüz gelmedi = they haven't come yet.
The suffix -dan/-den marks the source, 'from': Arkadaşımdan = from my friend.
Add -la/-le to a noun to make a manner adverb: mutluluk (happiness) plus -la gives mutlulukla = happily.
Verb stem plus -maya/-meye shows purpose, 'in order to': almaya = to buy, telling why you gittim (went).
yanında means 'next to'; the noun before it takes genitive -ın: fırının yanında = next to the bakery.
The suffix -acak/-ecek makes the future tense: yat- (go to bed) plus -acağım gives yatacağım = I will go to bed.
yakın (near) needs the dative -a/-e on what you are near: Denize yakın = close to the sea.
etmek turns a noun into a verb: ziyaret (a visit) plus ettik gives ziyaret ettik = we visited.
mı is the yes/no question word; it stays separate and sits after the thing asked about: araban mı = is it your car.
The suffix -malı/-meli means 'must/should': olmalıyız = we should be, söylememeliyiz = we shouldn't say.
In a noun-plus-noun compound the second noun takes -i: tatil (holiday) plus ev gives tatil evi = holiday house.
Put en before an adjective for the superlative 'most': en güzel = the most beautiful.
Add -ki after a locative to mean 'the one at/in': vitrinindeki = the one in the shop window.
The suffix -li/-lı means 'having': güneş (sun) plus -li gives güneşli = sunny.
The ending -sın gives a third-person command, 'let him/her': oynasın = let him play.
After a number, -lik means 'consisting of / sized for': beş kişilik = of five people (five-person).
Possession links two suffixes: the owner takes -ın, the thing takes -ı: Halasının evi = his aunt's house.
ayrılmak (to leave) takes the ablative -den on the place: hastaneden ayrıldı = left the hospital.
The suffix -mış reports something inferred from evidence, not witnessed: ıslanmış = they have gotten wet (I see the result).
Verb stem plus -ınca/-ince means 'when/upon doing': bakınca = when you look.
-mış on your own action marks a sudden realization: unutmuşum = oh, I've forgotten (I just noticed).
The aorist -ar/-er states habits and general truths: kalkar = gets up, bakar = tends, done regularly.
The negative aorist -emez/-amaz means 'cannot' and often 'not allowed': içemezsiniz = you can't smoke.
For comparisons use daha (more) and mark the standard with -dan: Ankara'dan daha kalabalık = more crowded than Ankara.
Infinitive plus için means 'in order to': önlemek için = in order to prevent.
